title: Capacity trim — sundown jotter
content:
Sundown shift notes — quick personal checklist and context for tonight

Context:
- Overnight batch backlog has been creeping after the new model rollout (smaller batches but more concurrent requests). Want to trim tails and reclaim idle GPUs for daytime canary.
- Watchlist: pool gpu-pool-3 (asia-west), preempt pressure on p4s, intermittent net spikes (pkt drops) seen ~02:00 PST last two nights.

Immediate goals (priority order):
1) Trim long-running low-priority batch jobs (estimate 30–45m)
   - Identify batches older than 6h in queue (queue name: batch-runner-prod).
   - Kill or requeue to low-priority bucket if they are in retry loop.
   - Commands: kubectl get pods -n batch -l job=batch-runner -o wide | grep Evicted/CrashLoop; kubectl delete pod <id> --grace-period=0 --force

2) Reclaim idle GPUs in gpu-pool-3 (asia-west)
   - Check node utilization: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv` on nodes via ssh bastion (quick script under /home/rhea/bin/gpu-idle-check).
   - If < 5% for > 20m and no KV cache pinned, drain node and cordon.
   - Drain: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` then annotate for reclaim.

3) Network tier sanity check (if pkt drops > 0.5%):
   - Check flow logs (gcloud/eth tool) for anomalous retransmits across infra-lb.
   - Restart envoy sidecar on affected pods (small blast radius canary).

4) Cost quicksight + billing check (10m)
   - Look at last 48h token spend vs expected after quantization changes. Flag anything >15% delta to finance slack.

Housekeeping / handoff notes to leave for morning: 
- Left a canary node (gpu-canary-07) uncordoned intentionally to absorb small traffic if reclaim delayed.
- Created short runbook gist for ops on how to undo a mistaken drain (link below).
- Marked INFRA-4821 as "awaiting night validation" on ticket.

Unresolved questions / action items to follow up:
- Why is preempt rate higher in asia-west only? (open hypothesis: scheduler config + lower demand grouping). Need SRE to look at eviction logs.
- Are prefix caches being warmed correctly after draining? Need to patch warm-up script to re-populate top-50 prefixes on restart.

Quick timeline + timeboxing for tonight:
- 21:15 — assess queue depth and list candidates (~10m)
- 21:25 — start trimming long batches (21:25–22:00)
- 22:00 — begin node drains (one at a time) (22:00–23:00)
- 23:00 — run network checks, restart envoy canary (23:00–23:20)
- 23:20 — billing + quicksight look, finalize notes (23:20–23:40)

Quick commands / snippets (save for next time):
- list pods by runtime: `kubectl get pods -n batch -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,AGE:.metadata.creationTimestamp,ST:.status.phase`
- drain with recheck: `kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
- check GPU usage across pool: simple loop `for n in $(nodes); do ssh $n "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv"; done`

Notes to self (less formal):
- Don’t be trigger-happy deleting jobs — if it’s in a retry window, requeue lower priority instead.
- If I see >2% pkt drops and more than one node, escalate to SRE and page on-call.
- Remember to update the warm-up script PR after morning verification.

Links / refs:
- INFRA-4821 (ticket) — notes attached about pool reclaim plan
- PR: serving-runtime#1293 — quantization rollouts and cache behavior (needs verification)
- Runbook gist: https://gist.github.com/rheapatel/xxxxxxxx

End-of-shift handoff blurb for morning: 
- "Left 2 drains in progress (nodes: gpu-03-azw, gpu-09-azw). Took out 7 long-running batch pods, requeued 4 to low-priority. Watch batch-runner backlog and prefix cache warming. Billing delta flagged under INFRA-4821. If nodes fail to rejoin by 07:30, escalate to SRE. — Rhea"

Random todo I keep forgetting: check scheduler sizing for low-priority queue (maybe increase backoff).
